site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full tessera system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Tessera documentation site features a robust three-column layout with clear information hierarchy, but suffers from significant mobile usability and accessibility gaps. Critical issues include horizontal overflow on mobile viewports that truncates operator tables, sub-44px tap targets for global navigation controls, and an unlabeled version switcher. Additionally, the primary 'Get started' CTA is a non-functional placeholder, breaking the initial user journey.

exploration_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of the Tessera documentation site, focusing on information architecture, navigation consistency, and the usability of technical reference pages (SQL/Functions) across desktop and mobile viewports.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will start at the homepage to validate global navigation and theme/version controls. It will then traverse the primary 'Reference' flow, testing the deep-linking TOC and specific function pages (`DATE_TRUNC`, `JSON_EXTRACT`) for content layout and readability. Finally, it will verify SQL syntax pages and repeat critical checks on mobile to address known tap-target risks.
assumptions: The 'Tutorials', 'Download', and 'GitHub' links in the header are placeholders (#) or external, so exploration will focus on internal docs/reference pages.
The left-hand TOC on reference pages is interactive (expand/collapse) as indicated by the prescan description.
The version switcher and theme toggle persist across all internal pages.
risk_hotspots: Global Header: Version switcher lacks accessible labels; multiple tap targets < 44px height.
Reference Page: Deep nested TOC navigation and sticky behavior on scroll.
Function Pages: Code block readability and 'Version History' collapsible panel interaction.
Mobile Viewport: High density of small tap targets in the header and TOC.

phases.title: Homepage & Global Controls
phases.objective: Validate entry point clarity, global navigation persistence, and utility controls (Search, Theme, Version).
key_checks: Verify 'Get Started' and 'View Reference' CTAs lead to expected destinations.
Toggle Dark/Light theme and observe visual state change and persistence.
Interact with Version Switcher (v2.4/v2.3/etc) to check dropdown behavior.
Trigger Command-K Search modal to verify overlay and input focus.
exit_criteria: Theme toggle visually updates the UI.
Search modal opens and accepts input.
All main nav links are clickable.

phases.title: Reference Architecture & Navigation
phases.objective: Assess the usability of the three-column reference layout and deep-linking TOC.
key_checks: Expand/Collapse nodes in the left-hand TOC (e.g., Functions > Aggregate).
Click a popular link (e.g., 'DATE_TRUNC') to test deep linking.
Scroll the center content pane to verify if the right-hand 'On this page' outline updates active state.
Check responsiveness of the three-column layout when resizing window.
exit_criteria: TOC nodes expand/collapse without layout shift errors.
Internal links navigate correctly to specific function pages.
Right-hand outline highlights current section on scroll.

phases.title: Technical Content & Function Details
phases.objective: Critique the presentation of complex technical data (signatures, params, examples) on specific function pages.
key_checks: Validate code block syntax highlighting and copy-to-clipboard functionality (if present).
Interact with 'Version History' collapsible panel at the bottom of the page.
Verify table readability for 'Parameters' and 'Return Value' sections.
Check breadcrumb navigation ('> FUNCTIONS > DATE / TIME') for correct hierarchy and clickability.
exit_criteria: Code blocks are legible and distinct from body text.
Version history panel toggles open/closed smoothly.

phases.title: SQL Syntax & Data Types
phases.objective: Ensure consistent styling and navigation for broader concept pages compared to specific function pages.
key_checks: Review 'SELECT' statement syntax diagram/table for horizontal overflow handling.
Check 'Data Types' table for responsive behavior (stacking vs scrolling).
Verify that 'Edit this page on GitHub' links are present and consistent.
Test back-navigation to Reference home via sidebar or breadcrumbs.
exit_criteria: Wide tables/code blocks do not break mobile layout (horizontal scroll available).
Navigation back to parent categories works intuitively.

phases.title: Mobile Validation & Accessibility
phases.objective: Re-run critical flows on mobile viewport to address prescan warnings regarding tap targets and layout.
key_checks: Verify header hamburger menu (if applicable) or horizontal scroll behavior for nav links.
Attempt to tap small header controls (Theme, Version) to assess error rate/usability.
Check if the left-hand TOC collapses into a drawer or remains visible on narrow screens.
Validate font sizes for code blocks and parameter tables on mobile.
exit_criteria: No critical layout breakage on mobile viewport.
Identification of specific 'fat finger' issues in the header and TOC.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise Theme Toggle, Version Switcher, Search Modal, TOC Expand/Collapse, Collapsible Panels.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1, 2, and 3 checks on mobile viewport (width < 768px).

notes: Prescan indicates missing aria-labels on the version switcher; note this in accessibility findings.
Many header tap targets are reported < 44px; prioritize observing actual user difficulty here during mobile phase.
The 'Tutorials' and 'Download' links appear to be stubs (#); do not spend time debugging broken links there unless they unexpectedly navigate.

findings.user_goal: Read technical reference tables on a mobile device
findings.problem: Horizontal overflow causes content truncation on mobile screens (viewport width 390px vs page width 465px).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in steps 73-80 indicate 'Page width 465px exceeds viewport 390px'. The final screenshot shows the 'Precedence' column of the Operators table cut off at the right edge, requiring horizontal scrolling to view full data.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices cannot see complete technical data (e.g., operator precedence or result columns) without manual horizontal scrolling, which is often undiscoverable and frustrating in vertical-scrolling contexts.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive table design: enable horizontal scrolling within the table container with a visual indicator, or stack/abbreviate less critical columns on narrow viewports.

findings.user_goal: Begin using the database via the homepage Call-to-Action
findings.problem: The primary 'Get started' button is a dead link (href='#').
findings.evidence: In steps 37-42 and 61-66, clicking 'Get started' only appended a hash fragment to the URL without navigating to installation or quickstart content. The agent noted this as a 'broken or placeholder user journey'.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the most prominent action on the landing page. Failing to guide new users to onboarding content creates immediate friction and increases bounce rates for first-time visitors.
findings.suggestion: Link the 'Get started' button to the 'Install' or 'Your first query' section/card identified in the homepage hero area.

findings.user_goal: Switch documentation versions using screen reader or keyboard navigation
findings.problem: The version switcher dropdown lacks an accessible label, aria-label, or placeholder text.
findings.evidence: Multiple layout warnings (steps 25-30, 43-48, 67-72) flag 'missing_input_label' for the version selector (ux-2/ux-7). The DOM summary confirms the select element has no associated label.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will hear 'combo box' or similar generic descriptions without context, making it difficult to understand the control's purpose or current state.
findings.suggestion: Add an aria-label='Select documentation version' or visually hidden label to the <select> element.

findings.user_goal: Interact with global navigation controls on touch devices
findings.problem: Multiple header tap targets are below the recommended 44x44px minimum size.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently identify small targets: 'Tessera' logo (100x26px), Theme toggle (42x37px), and Version switcher height (33px). Steps 67-72 confirmed these persist in mobile viewport.
findings.why_it_matters: Small touch targets lead to accidental taps and frustration, particularly for the theme toggle and version switcher which are frequently used utility controls.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding or hit-area of these buttons to meet the 44x44px WCAG/mobile guideline, even if the visual icon remains smaller.

findings.user_goal: Close the search modal when the close button is not obvious
findings.problem: The search modal lacks a visible 'X' close button, relying on clicking outside or keyboard shortcuts.
findings.evidence: In steps 73-78, the agent noted 'No explicit close button... is visible'. The agent had to use the Escape key (step 79) to recover when clicking the background failed initially due to overlay interception issues.
findings.why_it_matters: While keyboard users can use Escape, touch users may struggle to find the dismissal mechanism if tapping the dimmed background doesn't register immediately or isn't intuitive.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible 'X' icon in the top-right corner of the search modal for clear affordance.

gaps: Only directly exercised 6% of visible interactive feature signatures.
7 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
42% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
